chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Sama'ah from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Ali ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who bequeathed one-third of his wealth to his paternal uncles and maternal uncles, he said: 'For his paternal uncles, two-thirds, and for his maternal uncles, one-third.'
ai.seo_question: How is the one-third bequest distributed between paternal and maternal uncles in Shia inheritance law?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the distribution of the *wasiyyah* (bequest) portion, distinguishing between paternal and maternal uncles based on their respective shares in the fixed inheritance (*fara'id*). It reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle that the bequest to relatives follows the proportional distribution of their inheritance shares, thereby integrating the discretionary bequest with the structured laws of succession. This ruling is significant for understanding how Shia fiqh balances the one-third limit of the bequest with the rights of extended family members.
